rv.q: Oh, Mary! is outrageous, inventive, hysterically funny, and unlike almost anything else currently touring.
Cole Escola’s wildly absurd, historically inaccurate farce has made its way from Broadway to the national tour, and the transition works beautifully.
Alaska's Mary is glitzy, unpredictable and laugh-out-loud funny, but she is also more relatable—and more perceptive—than she initially lets on.
It is offensive and raunchy in the best way possible.
Oh, Mary! more than lives up to its reputation.
As feisty and foul-mouthed and queer and outrageous as “Oh, Mary!” ecstatically is, small theaters will be clamoring to do this show for decades.
But I can say I've never heard an audience at the Civic Theatre roar with more suprised laughter than I did on on Wednesday, the official opening night of the Broadway play's national tour.
Oh, Mary! was unlike anything I'd seen onstage before.
I loved every laugh-filled moment of it.

The play, a 2025. Pulitzer Prize in Drama finalist, is mighty bold and wonderfully irreverent, following a fictional, highly inaccurate version of the first lady in the weeks leading up to Abraham Lincoln's assassination.
The intense campiness that permeates the production is marvelously good fun...
What's brilliant about Escola's tightly constructed, 75-minute play is that, even with all the raunchy jokes and camp sensibility, it sits just on the edgier fringe of mainstream humor...
"Oh, Mary!" delivers plenty of chuckles but few belly laughs.
Oh, Mary! is a farcical delight that revels in the incredible comic timing of underrated drag queen Alaska Thunderfuck.

cn.t: Critics hail this irreverent farce as a raucously funny triumph, with Alaska Thunderfuck's star turn earning widespread praise. One dissenting voice finds it merely "so-so," but most agree it's a gleefully unhinged, bawdy delight.
